pages.title: Years 1 and 2: build the base
pages.note: A general plan for applying the summer after junior year; many people take gap years, and that's totally normal. Prerequisites vary by school, so check the AAMC's MSAR for the schools you like.

items: Meet your prehealth advisor
Map your prerequisite courses with them
Find study habits that work before adding more
Join one or two clubs you actually like
Start an activity log: dates, hours, a contact
Try one clinical role (volunteer, scribe, CNA, EMT...)
Keep a short journal of patient moments
Look into research labs if you're curious
Stay with the activities you care about
Add non-clinical service you'd do anyway
Shadow a few physicians, in different fields
Get to know 2-3 professors (future letters!)
Check your GPA trend; get help early if it dips
Keep your clinical role going (steady beats a burst)
Try research, a job or a program that interests you
Update your activity log and journal
Rest, too! Summers count as recovery
Apply for the AAMC Fee Assistance Program first, if eligible
Plan your MCAT date with room for a retake
Ask for letters with your CV and an early deadline
Start a list of schools in MSAR
Take the MCAT (2027 fee: $360, $145 with FAP)
Draft your personal statement (5,300 characters)
Write your Work and Activities (up to 15)
Pre-write common secondary prompts
AMCAS opens in early May (May 5 in 2027)
Submit early in the window (from May 28 in 2027)
Turn secondaries around in about 2 weeks
Interview season: practice out loud
Keep your activities going (they still count!)
Send updates where schools allow them
Decisions in spring: compare cost, aid and fit
Protect your sleep and your grades
Log hours the same week you do them
Do things you'd do even if med school weren't the goal

pins.headline: The premed roadmap, year by year
items: Freshman: advisor, prereqs, study habits
Sophomore: steady clinical + service
Junior: letters, MCAT, personal statement
Summer: submit AMCAS early
Senior: secondaries, interviews, decisions
